::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Can someone please explain to me why if the angle between z-a and z-(conjugate a) is acute then we can conclude that Re((z-a)(conjugate z-a))>0?](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/4595829/can-someone-please-explain-to-me-why-if-the-angle-between-z-a-and-z-conjugate-a), asked by [Whatever-_-](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/1129379/whatever) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2022-12-10; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> Here in that question https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/3793007/proof-of-jensens-theorem-on-roots-and-circles
> Thanks
:::

Outside of the context of the linked problem, the general statement is:

> The angle between $z$ and $w$ is acute iff $\Re(z\bar w) > 0$.

Thinking of $z$ and $w$ as vectors in the plane, the angle between them is acute if the dot product between them is positive. This is because $z \cdot w = |z| |w| \cos\theta$, where $\theta$ is the measure of the angle between $z$ and $w$. So $\cos\theta = \frac{z\cdot w}{|z||w|}$.  Therefore $\cos\theta > 0$ when $z \cdot w > 0$. The acute angles are the ones with positive cosine.

Now write $z = x_1 + i y_1$ and $w = x_2 + i y_2$. Then
$$z \cdot w = x_1x_2 + y_1 y_2$$
while
$$z \bar w = (x_1 + iy_1)(x_2 - iy_2)
    = (x_1 x_2 + y_1 y_2) + i(x_2 y_1 - x_1y_2)$$
So you see $z \cdot w = \Re(z\bar w)$.
